title: Where the balance guard lives
description: BAL-001 spans every mutating command. Weighed: guard built first in a dedicated story, or guard added last. Chose a shared guard in ledger-core used by each mutator, with BAL-001 as a late integration story that verifies the cross-command behavior.

options.label: Shared guard in ledger-core, integration story last
Add the guard only in the balance story

title: How to test database resolution under the shared acceptance store
description: Criteria may not replace DATABASE_URL or create temporary databases. Chose to unit-test the resolution function directly with explicit environment mappings and leave end-to-end resolution to the grader and the project's own suite.

options.label: Test resolver with injected environment mapping

title: Unstated response contracts
description: Malformed or empty arguments exit 2; duplicate keys inside a load file exit 3 with nothing written; a missing-tables database exits 1.
system_choice: Empty or malformed arguments exit 2, duplicate keys in a load exit 3, unreachable database or missing tables exit 1.

title: Duplicate command registration and pytest import path
description: register() raises ValueError on a duplicate word tuple rather than silently replacing the handler, so two command modules cannot shadow each other. I also added pythonpath = ["."] to pyproject.toml's pytest options so tests can import cli. Is that acceptable, or should the import path come from a conftest.py instead?

title: PostgreSQL driver dependency
description: Added psycopg[binary] to pyproject.toml via uv, as the stack contract and the driver's own error message require.

title: Two resolvers, one default each
description: cli.database.resolve_database_dsn returns the literal 'data/app.db' as the spec states. cli.config.resolve_dsn, required by the earlier FEATURE-CliEntry.md check, wraps it and substitutes the absolute application-root path for the default, so commands run from any directory. Is that acceptable, or should the two defaults be unified on replan?
system_choice: cli.database.resolve_database_dsn returns the literal 'data/app.db' as the spec states. cli.config.resolve_dsn, required by the earlier FEATURE-CliEntry.md check, wraps it and substitutes the absolute application-root path for the default, so commands run from any directory. Is that acceptable, or should the two defaults be unified on replan?

title: Init empties tables rather than dropping them
description: The story says drop and recreate, but the FEATURE Behavior says make sure the tables exist, then empty them in foreign-key order. I followed the Behavior. Tables are created from schema.sql only when a probe finds one missing, because execute_script is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction. Should init drop and recreate instead?

Tables are created from schema.sql only when a probe finds one missing, because execute_script is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction. Should init drop and recreate instead?

title: balance_guard on unknown accounts
description: balance_guard does not verify that an account exists; it computes the balance as zero for an unknown code. Existence checks belong to the calling commands. Is that acceptable, or should the guard reject unknown accounts?
system_choice: balance_guard does not verify that an account exists; it computes the balance as zero for an unknown code. Existence checks belong to the calling commands. Is that acceptable, or should the guard reject unknown accounts?

title: All-or-nothing writes
description: Same limitation as load transactions: validation completes before the first write, but a mid-write database failure can leave partial rows, because there is no transaction facility to wrap the writes. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: Same limitation as load transactions: validation completes before the first write, but a mid-write database failure can leave partial rows, because there is no transaction facility to wrap the writes. Is that acceptable?

title: All-or-nothing writes
description: Same limitation as the other loads. Categories also have no per-row delete declared, so no compensating undo is possible. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: Same limitation as the other loads. Categories also have no per-row delete declared, so no compensating undo is possible. Is that acceptable?

title: All-or-nothing writes
description: The spec asks for one transaction, but the persistence package exposes no multi-statement transaction to application code, and the rules forbid driver calls. I validate every row and the balance guard before the first write, so validation failures store nothing. A database error partway through the write phase can still leave earlier rows stored. Is that acceptable, or should the persistence layer add a transaction facility?
system_choice: The spec asks for one transaction, but the persistence package exposes no multi-statement transaction to application code, and the rules forbid driver calls. I validate every row and the balance guard before the first write, so validation failures store nothing. A database error partway through the write phase can still leave earlier rows stored. Is that acceptable, or should the persistence layer add a transaction facility?

title: File txn_id range
description: The spec says a non-integer txn_id is rejected but does not give a range. I accept only positive integers up to 2147483647, the INTEGER column limit, and reject 0 and negatives. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: The spec says a non-integer txn_id is rejected but does not give a range. I accept only positive integers up to 2147483647, the INTEGER column limit, and reject 0 and negatives. Is that acceptable?

title: Missing TRANSFER category
description: If the store has no TRANSFER category, transfer exits 1 as an operational failure rather than 3, since it is a store configuration problem rather than bad input. Is that acceptable?
system_choice: If the store has no TRANSFER category, transfer exits 1 as an operational failure rather than 3, since it is a store configuration problem rather than bad input. Is that acceptable?

title: Two-row atomicity
description: Both TRANSFER rows are checked before the first write, but the two creates are not wrapped in a transaction. A failure on the second create would leave the first stored. Is that acceptable, or should the persistence layer add a transaction facility?
system_choice: Both TRANSFER rows are checked before the first write, but the two creates are not wrapped in a transaction. A failure on the second create would leave the first stored. Is that acceptable, or should the persistence layer add a transaction facility?

title: Indexes derived from the persistence declaration
description: The rendered schema indexes transactions(account); transactions(category); transactions(account, category). Each is implied by the declaration — a foreign key is looked up by its child column, and a read pattern's Input fields are the predicate it filters on. Declare an `- INDEX (...)` bullet in DATABASE.md for any index this does not cover.
